definition: Pipelines that score and filter raw data: heuristics (length, symbol ratios), model-based quality classifiers, toxicity filters, and language identification.
details: Pipelines that score and filter raw data: heuristics (length, symbol ratios), model-based quality classifiers, toxicity filters, and language identification. Modern practice increasingly uses LLM-graded quality signals; data curation now rivals architecture as a competitive differentiator.

explainer.lead: Quality classifiers are the scoring and filtering stage of a data pipeline that decides which raw data is worth training on. They matter because data curation now rivals architecture as a competitive differentiator.

tiers.eli5: Before cooking, you sort through a pile of ingredients and throw out the bruised and spoiled ones — quality classifiers do that sorting for training data.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers stack heuristics such as length and symbol ratios with model-based quality scores, toxicity filters, and language identification, and increasingly use LLM-graded signals. A pitfall is over-filtering: aggressive thresholds can strip diversity and bias the resulting model.
tiers.paperLevel: A pipeline of scorers s(x) applied to each raw item, with filtering by threshold; no single formal definition exists, and thresholds trade data volume against data quality.

explainer.example: A crawl is passed through a language identifier, a toxicity filter, and a model-based quality scorer, and only documents above the quality threshold proceed to training.
